questions.q: Why would you spell out CALCULATE(<expr>, DATESYTD(<dates>)) instead of just using TOTALYTD?
options: TOTALYTD only accepts a single additional filter argument; spelling it out with CALCULATE lets you combine DATESYTD with as many other filters as needed
TOTALYTD is deprecated and no longer works
DATESYTD is always faster than TOTALYTD
TOTALYTD can only be used in calculated columns
questions.explain: Once you need two or more filter conditions alongside the year-to-date restriction, CALCULATE with DATESYTD spelled out gives you room for all of them — TOTALYTD's single optional filter argument isn't enough.

options: Every date between two specific dates you name, with no calendar pattern involved
Only the start and end dates themselves
A count of the days between two dates
The year-to-date total for a measure
questions.explain: Unlike DATEADD or DATESYTD, which follow calendar patterns (a year, a month), DATESBETWEEN just returns every date in a custom range you specify directly.

questions.q: In a life-to-date measure using DATESBETWEEN(dates, BLANK(), MAX(dates)), what does passing BLANK() as the start date do?
options: Tells DATESBETWEEN to use the earliest date in the table automatically
Causes the measure to return blank in every case
Removes the date filter entirely
Sets the start date to today's date
questions.explain: BLANK() as the StartDate argument means DATESBETWEEN defaults to the earliest date present in the dates column — the true beginning of the data.

questions.q: What does a life-to-date (LTD) measure represent?
options: A running total accumulated since the very beginning of the data, up to whatever end point the report is filtered to
The total for only the current day
The average value across the entire dataset
A total that resets every year like TOTALYTD
questions.explain: Life-to-date never resets — it keeps accumulating from day one of the data through the current filter context, unlike YTD/MTD/QTD which reset on a schedule.

questions.q: What's the common shape shared by every time intelligence function covered in this chapter?
options: Each produces a table of dates, passed to CALCULATE as a filter argument — time intelligence is CALCULATE applied to dates
Each one requires a calculated column, never a measure
Each one ignores filter context entirely
Each one only works with DirectQuery data sources
questions.explain: DATEADD, DATESYTD, DATESBETWEEN, and the TOTAL* shortcuts all boil down to building a table of dates that CALCULATE then filters by — the same CALCULATE pattern from Chapter 5, just applied specifically to dates.
